text: hey everybody this is a quick reminder that the term Immaculate Conception doesn't refer to the conception of Jesus it refers to the conception of Mary and
the idea that there is something special about the conception of Mary the mother of Jesus goes all the way back to the second century CE where we see it first
in the apocryphal Gospel of James where we get this idea that Mary's parents conceived her without sexual intercourse now this text was not considered
authoritative within the early Orthodox church but a number of church fathers discussed Mary's Purity and her
sinlessness because sex was still seen as something impure and even down to this day sex is commonly perceived as
something impure and something associated with base fleshly existence a very platonic view of these things in
the medieval period debates arose about how Mary could be sinless if she inherited original sin through the
sexual Union of her parents and this gave rise to a doctrine that held that there was something special about that
Union that made it so original sin was not present and that way Mary could be free from original sin and that Doctrine
which was mainly formalized over the last few centuries is what we know as the Immaculate Conception
